meanings.note: Bonne soirée = have a nice evening. Feminine noun ('la soirée', plural 'les soirées') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'evening'.
Une soirée = an evening party. Feminine noun ('la soirée', plural 'les soirées') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'evening'.
Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'solution, answer'.

examples.text: Une solution? Une grande actrice de quatre-vingts ans, libre dans trois semaines?
examples.trans: A solution? A great eighty-year-old actress, free in three weeks?

meanings.note: agrees with the thing owned, not the owner

examples.text: Oui, trois cent mille. Je parle de ses vingt ans de carrière.
examples.trans: Yes, three hundred thousand. I'm talking about his twenty years of career.

meanings.note: Sur la table, sur la route. Core French preposition meaning 'on', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
Sur haut-parleur = on speaker. Core French preposition meaning 'on', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: Le livre est sur la table.

examples.text: Attention, tu arrives sur la route!

meanings.note: Je suis sérieuse = I mean it. French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Je suis sérieuse. J'ai toujours adoré le cinéma.
examples.trans: I'm serious. I've always loved films.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la taxe', plural 'les taxes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'tax'.

examples.text: Une nouvelle taxe sur les acteurs français.
examples.trans: A new tax on French actors.

examples.text: Laquelle? On pourrait dire qu'il y a une nouvelle taxe sur les acteurs français?
examples.trans: Which one? Could we say there's a new tax on French actors?

meanings.note: The document saying who inherits. Masculine action/result noun formed with the Romance suffix '-ment' (from Latin '-mentum'). Standard masculine noun meaning 'will'.

examples.text: Il n'a pas laissé de testament.
Merci. Samuel n'a pas laissé de testament.
examples.trans: Thank you. Samuel didn't leave a will.

meanings.note: Tout le monde = everybody. Spoken French det expression meaning 'all', common in natural conversation.

meanings.en: tout ce que = all that, everything that
meanings.note: Pronoun use. Spoken French det expression meaning 'all', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: C'est tout ce que je peux faire.
Désolé, c'est tout ce que je peux faire.
examples.trans: Sorry, that's all I can do.

meanings.note: takes a singular verb: tout le monde est là

examples.text: On est au Westin. Tout le monde est là.
examples.trans: We're at the Westin. Everyone is here.

meanings.note: trouver quelqu'un sympa = to find someone nice

meanings.en: trouve quelque chose = think of something
meanings.note: In context. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to find'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'trouvé').

examples.text: Je ne sais pas. Trouve quelque chose.
examples.trans: I don't know. Think of something.

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'very'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Très bien. Et vous? Un thé?

Number; l'un = one of them. Spoken French det expression meaning 'a', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: L'un à midi, l'autre à deux heures.
examples.trans: One at noon, the other at two.

meanings.note: En vente = for sale, on sale. Feminine noun ('la vente', plural 'les ventes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'sale'.

examples.text: Tout le monde est au courant que l'agence est en vente.
examples.trans: Everyone knows that the agency is for sale.

meanings.note: n'avoir rien à voir avec = to have nothing to do with
Voir quelqu'un. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to see'.

examples.text: Magali, je dois voir la pièce de Koltès cette semaine.
examples.trans: Magali, I have to see the Koltès play this week.

meanings.note: + noun or infinitive. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to want'.
Imparfait, softer. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to want'.

examples.text: Je voulais te faire la surprise.
Je ne suis pas actrice. Je veux juste voir Mathias.
examples.trans: I'm not an actress. I just want to see Mathias.
